oneLiner: Retrofit autonomy for existing aircraft: a $105M-ceiling USSOCOM C-130J program, USAF KC-135 flight testing, and a first-of-its-kind NZ/FAA certification path -- trading near $4 with $183.9M cash and a $32M revenue promise its $2M quarters have not yet met.
thesis: The certification lead is real and rare. Merlin completed SOI 1 and SOI 2 with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand working in partnership with the FAA, and on Aug 6, 2026 announced SOI 3 for the Flight Control Computer and Automated Communication System, plus an agreed approach to certifying AI/ML natural-language components -- a first for the category.

Defense anchors the model while civil matures. The prime IDIQ with USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy carries a $105M ceiling, and the critical design review was completed Jun 4, 2026, moving the program into aircraft integration. KC-135 automation work with the USAF (agreement Feb 2024, flight testing with partner SNC since 2025) extends the tanker-fleet opportunity.

Aircraft-agnostic software is the scaling story. Merlin executed its first fully automated fixed-wing takeoffs on Apr 11 and Apr 21, 2026 (one in the US, one in New Zealand) and demonstrated an autonomous landing at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh on Jul 20, 2026; the Condor product family (announced May 14, 2026) extends Merlin Pilot to large multi-crew cargo and military aircraft.

The SPAC hangover is the price. Merlin listed Mar 17, 2026 via Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. IV at a ~$800M valuation with ~$200M of fresh capital; the stock has fallen from a $17 high to roughly $4 (it closed Aug 13 at $4.42, then dropped ~10% after hours on the Q2 print), and targets were cut through July (Roth $15 to $10, TD Cowen $11 to $8) even as all four analysts stay at Buy.

Funding is adequate near term. Cash, equivalents and short-term investments were $183.9M with no debt at Jun 30, 2026, against a $27.8M adjusted EBITDA loss in Q2 -- roughly six quarters of runway at the current burn rate.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 13) doubled revenue sequentially to $2.2M -- almost all defense program work -- but missed the ~$3.8M consensus, and the $(58.4)M GAAP loss was again mostly non-cash fair-value noise from SPAC-related instruments. The operating reality: adjusted EBITDA burn widened to $(27.8)M from $(23.3)M in Q1 as certification and program spending ramped, operating cash flow was $(27.3)M, and cash ended at $183.9M with no debt. Alongside the print, Merlin disclosed a non-binding MOU with Israel Aerospace Industries for AI-powered autonomy and showcased the Oshkosh autonomous landing. Shares rose 6.3% into the report and gave back ~10% after hours. The disclosure that matters most: first-half revenue totaled $3.2M against the ~$32M full-year projection shown to SPAC investors -- the credibility gap is now arithmetic, not interpretation.
guidanceProse: Merlin still issues no formal guidance; the IPO deck's ~$32M 2026 revenue projection is effectively dead after a $3.2M first half, and management steered the Q2 call toward milestones (C-130J integration, KC-135 testing, NZ certification) rather than numbers. Funding remains solid but the clock ticks faster: $183.9M of cash, no debt, and a burn rate now near $28M a quarter imply roughly six quarters of runway before new capital is needed. The central debate is unchanged -- whether defense task orders and SOI-stage certification progress convert into contracted revenue fast enough to justify a ~$390M market cap -- but the Q2 burn acceleration moves the funding wall from a 2028 question toward late 2027. Sell-side remains Buy-rated with targets far above the ~$4 share price.

segments: Defense: USSOCOM C-130J autonomy prime IDIQ ($105M ceiling; CDR complete Jun 2026, now in aircraft integration), USAF KC-135 automation flight testing with SNC, UAE opportunity scoping via the Remah International Group teaming agreement (Apr 23, 2026), and a non-binding MOU with Israel Aerospace Industries for AI-powered autonomy (disclosed Aug 13, 2026).

Civil: Merlin Pilot certification through NZ CAA with FAA coordination (SOI 3 achieved Aug 2026), targeting the first certified fully automated takeoff-to-touchdown fixed-wing flight; Condor for large cargo aircraft with a non-binding World Star Aviation MOU.
Essentially all reported revenue today is program and development work, not product sales.
competitive: Reliable Robotics is the closest comparable: Cessna Caravan continuous-autopilot STC path with the FAA plus its own USAF work -- arguably ahead on the US civil certification route, though still private.
Joby (JOBY) absorbed Xwing's autonomy division in 2024 and pairs a similar superpilot ambition with a multi-billion-dollar balance sheet spanning air taxis and defense.
Shield AI's Hivemind owns the combat-autonomy narrative at multi-billion private valuations, but targets uncrewed tactical jets rather than retrofit cargo and tanker autonomy.
Primes and incumbents bound the space: Lockheed/Sikorsky MATRIX, Airbus autonomy programs, and Garmin Autoland at the low end.

Versus platform peers Kratos (KTOS) and AeroVironment (AVAV), Merlin sells certified software retrofits for existing airframes rather than new unmanned aircraft -- a smaller market today, but capital-light if certification lands first.
moat: The certification archive is the intended moat: SOI 3 with the NZ CAA and an agreed pathway for certifying AI/ML-based components genuinely leads most rivals, and regulators move slowly for followers too. But nothing is certified yet, revenue runs ~$1M a quarter, the World Star and Remah agreements are non-binding, and a defense IDIQ ceiling is not backlog. Until a certified product ships or task orders convert, the moat is a well-documented head start, not a business.
risks: Commercialization gap: $3.2M of first-half revenue against ~$32M projected for 2026 in SPAC materials; the Q2 miss ($2.2M vs ~$3.8M consensus) shows even reset expectations are hard to hit.

Certification risk: SOI 3 covers two components; full takeoff-to-touchdown certification, FAA validation of the NZ path, and operational approvals for AI/ML systems remain unproven ground for any regulator.
Defense concentration and IDIQ optics: the $105M C-130J ceiling is a maximum, not contracted revenue; USSOCOM priorities, budgets, and timelines can shift.

Burn: the adjusted EBITDA loss accelerated to $27.8M in Q2 from $23.3M in Q1, pointing to a funding wall around late 2027 absent revenue inflection; the $80M PIPE arrived barely six weeks after listing.
Competition from better-funded players: Joby/Xwing, Shield AI, Reliable Robotics, and the primes can outspend Merlin many times over.
Post-SPAC technicals: the stock has traversed $17.00 to $3.27 in five months and dropped ~10% after hours on the Q2 print; lockup expiries and warrant overhang can cap rallies and amplify drawdowns.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results, expected ~November 2026: first quarter where the market looks for evidence of C-130J integration-phase work billing at scale.
First certified fully automated takeoff-to-touchdown fixed-wing flight with the NZ CAA (company target; watch H2 2026 into 2027).
C-130J aircraft-integration milestones and potential USSOCOM task orders through 2026-27.
KC-135 flight-test campaign progress with USAF/SNC and any movement toward a program of record in the FY2027-28 budget cycle.
Condor commercialization: converting the World Star Aviation MOU to a definitive agreement; outcomes from the UAE (Remah) teaming.
pricedIn: At roughly $4.00 (Aug 13 after-hours print; late-August price unverified) on ~96.5M shares, market cap is ~$390M; net of $183.9M cash, enterprise value is roughly $205M against ~$9M of TTM revenue (estimated) -- nominally ~23x sales, but the market is pricing programs, not revenue. The stock has lost ~77% from its $17 March 2026 high, so SPAC froth is largely wrung out; four analysts still average a $9.75 target. What is priced in: continued defense execution and eventual certification, with little near-term revenue. The debate after Q2: whether accelerating burn ($27.8M adjusted EBITDA loss) buys enough certification and integration progress before the roughly six-quarter runway forces either revenue inflection or dilution.

scenarios.bear: Q2's pattern repeats: revenue stays in the low single-digit millions, burn holds near $28M a quarter, and the $32M 2026 projection is quietly abandoned. Certification grinds -- flight-test evidence for AI/ML components takes years -- while USSOCOM task orders stay small and Condor remains an MOU. By late 2027 cash is under $60M, forcing a dilutive raise at depressed prices. The stock breaks its $3.27 low and settles toward cash value, roughly $2-3, as the market reclassifies Merlin as a funded lab rather than a product company.
scenarios.base: Defense revenue ramps as C-130J integration converts to billable task orders and KC-135 testing advances; 2026 revenue lands far below the $32M projection (perhaps $8-12M off a $3.2M first half) but roughly doubles into 2027. The first certified automated flight arrives within about a year, validating the NZ CAA path. Burn moderates as programs bill. The stock ranges $4-8, re-rating on each contract or certification headline, with the late-2027 funding question deferred rather than answered.
scenarios.bull: Certification lands: a certified takeoff-to-touchdown automated flight in late 2026 or 2027 makes Merlin the civil fixed-wing autonomy first mover, pulling Condor commitments from cargo operators and lessors. USSOCOM spends toward the full $105M ceiling and a KC-135 program of record emerges from the 2027 budget. Revenue exceeds $50M in 2027 on defense margins, and strategic interest from primes puts a floor under the story. The stock revisits $10-15 -- analyst-target territory -- without needing SPAC-era froth.

valPresets.note: Revenue mode because GAAP earnings are distorted by SPAC fair-value marks (Q2 GAAP loss $58.4M vs $27.8M adjusted EBITDA loss) and FCF is deeply negative. TTM revenue (~$9M estimated) is a tiny, lumpy program-revenue base, so implied CAGRs look extreme -- read them as the growth defense task orders plus certified-product sales would need to justify the price, not as forecasts.
